body.objective: Extend the finite cyclic homological layer from checking q2/q3 identities to deciding invariant interaction content: deformation complexes, Maurer-Cartan equations modulo admissible cyclic L-infinity redefinitions, obstruction classes and bounded-order miniversal bases. The immediate consumers are sf:program/work/nonlinear-cyclic-deformation-class-completeness and sf:program/work/nonlinear-conflux-branch-mixing-discovery. The programme can presently certify a retained interaction and exhibit selected shears, but it cannot generically decide whether a mixed bracket is a nonzero operation on cohomology, a nontrivial cyclic deformation class, or a removable presentation artifact.
body.stop_condition: Represent finite graded symmetric coalgebras, coderivations, cyclic pairings, Nijenhuis-Richardson/Gerstenhaber brackets and arity filtrations over exact fields. Construct the deformation differential ad_Q, exact cocycle/coboundary spaces, induced operations on cohomology, obstruction brackets, gauge/redefinition orbits and a miniversal Maurer-Cartan base through a declared finite arity/order. Return explicit witnesses for nontriviality, trivializing cyclic L-infinity morphisms when they exist, or UNDECIDED outside the finite carrier. Reproduce the repaired q2 cyclic convention, classify the current mixed q3 representative through the first and second jet redefinition spaces, and decide one branch-resolved coefficient as invariant or removable. Independently replay all morphism, cyclicity and obstruction identities from the emitted maps. Export cohomology classes, orbit representatives and unresolved moduli to Conflux without allowing a low-cost normal form to stand in for an equivalence proof.
body.forbid: no retained representative called a physical interaction before quotienting admissible redefinitions; no finite arity computation called an all-order theorem; no parity-only cyclic convention substituted for the declared odd Darboux polarization; no basis-dependent coefficient called invariant; no producer basis reused as the independent cohomology verifier; no physics branch labels hard-coded into generic deformation algebra
